Aurelia Skyways Companion Animal Travel Desk

We acknowledge your complaint regarding the handling of Skye during your connection, and the resulting concern you raised about a delayed departure and a minor injury.

First, we are treating this as urgent operational feedback. Our ground team is required to move carriers carefully between services, verify secure placement before transfer, and confirm readiness with the next service point prior to departure. When a passenger reports distress or an incident involving a pet, the supervisor on duty must slow handoff steps to prevent further stress and to ensure the animal remains stable throughout the transfer window.

Second, on the claim timeline, <<FACT F119>>. This filing period matters because late submissions can delay validation and distribution of any appropriate outcome. If you have not already started the process, proceed immediately through the companion animal incident channel provided at the point of disruption, and attach any documentation you have from the travel day, including the status notes from ground staff and any vet observations that were made.

Third, we recognize that a delayed departure can cause cascading effects on carrier handling, holding areas, and the coordination of onward checks. <<FACT F109>>. That standard payout is the baseline outcome associated with the incident type you reported, but it also depends on the evidence available in your file, including the sequence of services and the time stamps recorded during operational handoff.

We also want to address your specific concern about the minor injury and why the response did not feel fast enough. Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried, and that includes immediately escalating to the operational desk so carrier handling can be paused or re-sequenced if the pet appears stressed or unwell. If the first responders on the ground did not reflect the correct priority level for your situation, that is an internal process failure and will be reviewed for corrective action with the transfer team.

If you are able to provide the incident description you submitted, including the points of transfer and the name of the attendant who interacted with you, the senior coordinator can reconcile the carrier movement logs against your account and complete the record without unnecessary delay.
